subject: titan triggerfish
title: This 30-Inch Fish Bites Scuba Divers, and Swimming Up Makes It Worse

scenes.text: This fish attacks scuba divers. And swimming up makes it worse.
The titan triggerfish, the biggest triggerfish on the reef: up to 75 centimetres, with chisel teeth built for cracking sea urchins and coral.
When it guards its nest, its territory is a cone that widens all the way up to the surface. Swim upward and you are still inside it.
Divers have had fins shredded, cameras bitten, a forearm, a thigh, and in Palau one man's ear cut clean through.
The escape is sideways. Swim horizontally and you leave the cone. Stay about 30 feet from a nest in spawning season.
Not venomous. No shark teeth. Just a fish that understands geometry better than you do.

description:
The titan triggerfish bites scuba divers who stray into its nesting territory, and because that territory is a cone widening up to the surface, swimming upward only keeps you inside it.
The titan triggerfish (Balistoides viridescens) grows to about 75 cm and crunches sea urchins, molluscs and coral with chisel-like teeth. Divers have reported bites to fins, cameras, forearms, thighs and in one case an ear cut through; the standard advice is to swim away horizontally and keep about 30 feet from nests during spawning, which is tied to the lunar cycle.
Have you ever been chased by a fish?
first_comment: A cone of water it will defend to the surface. Would you swim sideways, or panic and go up?
